messages.content: What is the Clojure style guide's recommendations for indentation?

The Clojure style guide recommends the following for indentation:

**Use 2 Spaces (No Tabs)**
```clojure
;; Good - 2 space indentation
(when something
  (something-else))

(defn my-fn [x]
  (let [y (+ x 1)]
    (* y 2)))

;; Bad - 4 spaces or tabs
(when something
    (something-else))
```

**Vertically Align Function Arguments**
```clojure
;; Good - aligned arguments
(defn send-email
  [to subject body]
  (send {:to to
         :subject subject
         :body body}))

;; Good - thread-first macro
(-> person
    (assoc :name "Alice")
    (update :age inc))

;; Good - map/filter arguments
(filter even?
        (range 10))
```

**Function Call Indentation**
```clojure
;; If first arg on same line, align others
(my-function arg1
             arg2
             arg3)

;; If first arg on new line, indent 2 spaces
(my-function
  arg1
  arg2
  arg3)
```

**Let Bindings**
```clojure
;; Good - aligned binding values
(let [name  "Alice"
      age   30
      email "alice@example.com"]
  (create-user name age email))

;; Also acceptable - no alignment
(let [name "Alice"
      age 30
      email "alice@example.com"]
  (create-user name age email))
```

**Map/Vector Indentation**
```clojure
;; Good - aligned values
{:name    "Alice"
 :age     30
 :country "USA"}

;; Good - one per line, values on same line as keys
{:name "Alice"
 :age 30
 :country "USA"}

;; Good - vectors
[1 2 3
 4 5 6
 7 8 9]
```

**Closing Parentheses**
```clojure
;; Good - closing parens together
(defn example []
  (when something
    (do-this)
    (do-that)))

;; Bad - closing parens on separate lines
(defn example []
  (when something
    (do-this)
    (do-that)
  )
)
```
What are the naming conventions in Clojure?

Clojure has specific naming conventions that make code more readable and predictable:

**kebab-case for Everything**
```clojure
;; Functions, variables, namespaces
(def user-count 42)
(defn calculate-total [items] ...)
(ns my-app.user-service)

;; NOT camelCase or snake_case
(def userCount 42)       ; Bad
(def user_count 42)      ; Bad
```

**Predicate Functions: question-mark?**
```clojure
;; Functions returning boolean end with ?
(defn valid? [x] ...)
(defn empty? [coll] ...)
(defn admin? [user] ...)
(defn can-edit? [user doc] ...)

;; Usage reads naturally
(when (valid? input)
  (process input))
```

**Side-Effect Functions: bang!**
```clojure
;; Functions with side effects end with !
(defn save! [data] ...)
(defn delete! [id] ...)
(defn send-email! [to body] ...)

;; State-modifying functions
(swap! atom inc)    ; Built-in
(reset! atom 0)     ; Built-in
```

**Dynamic Vars: *earmuffs***
```clojure
;; Dynamically rebindable vars use *earmuffs*
(def ^:dynamic *db-connection* nil)
(def ^:dynamic *current-user* nil)

;; Usage with binding
(binding [*db-connection* (get-connection)]
  (query *db-connection* "SELECT * FROM users"))
```

**Constants: No Special Convention**
```clojure
;; Just use regular names (all caps is NOT idiomatic)
(def max-retries 3)
(def default-timeout 5000)

;; NOT like Java
(def MAX_RETRIES 3)  ; Not idiomatic
```

**Private Functions: defn-**
```clojure
;; Use defn- for implementation details
(defn- helper-fn [x]
  (internal-logic x))

;; Or ^:private metadata
(def ^:private internal-state (atom {}))
```

**Conversion Functions: ->type and type->**
```clojure
;; Converting to a type: ->target
(defn ->json [data] ...)
(defn ->map [record] ...)

;; Converting from a type: source->
(defn json-> [s] ...)
(defn string->int [s] ...)

;; Records auto-generate these
(defrecord User [name email])
(->User "Alice" "a@b.com")     ; Positional constructor
(map->User {:name "Alice" :email "a@b.com"})  ; Map constructor
```

**Abbreviations**
```clojure
;; Common abbreviations
(ns myapp.core
  (:require [clojure.string :as str]  ; str is conventional
            [clojure.set :as set]      ; set is conventional
            [ring.util.response :as resp]))

;; Avoid single letters except in common contexts
(map (fn [x] (* x x)) coll)  ; x is OK for simple lambdas
(reduce (fn [acc item] ...) coll)  ; acc, item are descriptive
```

**Namespace Names**
```clojure
;; project.module.submodule format
(ns myapp.core)           ; Entry point
(ns myapp.api.handlers)   ; API handlers
(ns myapp.db.users)       ; User DB operations

;; Test namespaces
(ns myapp.core-test)      ; Tests for myapp.core
```
What are some Clojure idioms I should follow for cleaner code?

Here are essential Clojure idioms for writing cleaner, more idiomatic code:

**Prefer Threading Macros**
```clojure
;; Bad - nested calls
(str (+ (* 3 5) 10) " items")

;; Good - thread-first for transformations
(-> 5
    (* 3)
    (+ 10)
    (str " items"))

;; Good - thread-last for sequences
(->> (range 10)
     (filter even?)
     (map #(* % %)))
```

**Use when Instead of (if x y nil)**
```clojure
;; Bad
(if condition
  (do-something)
  nil)

;; Good
(when condition
  (do-something))

;; Similarly, use when-not instead of (if (not x) y nil)
(when-not condition
  (do-something))
```

**Use if-let and when-let**
```clojure
;; Bad
(let [result (find-user id)]
  (if result
    (process result)
    (handle-not-found)))

;; Good
(if-let [result (find-user id)]
  (process result)
  (handle-not-found))

;; Good - when-let for single branch
(when-let [user (find-user id)]
  (send-email user))
```

**Prefer Keyword Lookup Over get**
```clojure
;; OK
(get user :name)

;; Better - keywords as functions
(:name user)
(:email user "default@example.com")  ; with default

;; Maps as functions (less common)
(user :name)
```

**Use into for Collection Conversion**
```clojure
;; Convert to different collection type
(into [] '(1 2 3))      ; => [1 2 3]
(into #{} [1 2 2 3])    ; => #{1 2 3}
(into {} [[:a 1] [:b 2]])  ; => {:a 1, :b 2}

;; With transducer
(into []
      (comp (filter even?) (map inc))
      (range 10))
```

**Prefer comp and partial**
```clojure
;; Instead of nested anonymous functions
(map #(keyword (str/lower-case %)) names)

;; Use comp for function composition
(map (comp keyword str/lower-case) names)

;; Use partial for partial application
(def add-tax (partial * 1.08))
(add-tax 100)  ; => 108.0
```

**Avoid Anonymous Functions for Named Operations**
```clojure
;; Bad - anonymous function wrapping named function
(map #(inc %) numbers)
(filter #(even? %) numbers)

;; Good - use the function directly
(map inc numbers)
(filter even? numbers)

;; Anonymous functions are fine for complex operations
(map #(+ (:price %) (* (:quantity %) (:unit-price %))) items)
```

**Use Destructuring Liberally**
```clojure
;; Bad
(defn process-user [user]
  (let [name (get user :name)
        email (get user :email)]
    ...))

;; Good
(defn process-user [{:keys [name email]}]
  ...)

;; With defaults and :as
(defn create-server [{:keys [port host] 
                      :or {port 8080 host "localhost"}
                      :as config}]
  ...)
```

**Use Multiple Arities for Defaults**
```clojure
;; Good - clear default behavior
(defn greet
  ([name] (greet "Hello" name))
  ([greeting name] (str greeting ", " name "!")))

;; For many optional args, use a map
(defn create-user
  [name & {:keys [email role active?]
           :or {role :user active? true}}]
  {:name name :email email :role role :active? active?})

(create-user "Alice" :email "a@b.com" :role :admin)
```

**Prefer condp for Multi-Way Conditionals**
```clojure
;; Instead of nested if/cond with same predicate
(condp = status
  :pending "Waiting..."
  :active  "Running"
  :done    "Complete"
  "Unknown")  ; default

(condp < score
  90 "A"
  80 "B"
  70 "C"
  "F")
```

**Use case for Constant Dispatch**
```clojure
;; Faster than condp for compile-time constants
(case color
  :red   "#FF0000"
  :green "#00FF00"
  :blue  "#0000FF"
  "#000000")  ; default
```
What are the recommended line length and whitespace rules in Clojure?

Here are the whitespace and line length conventions for Clojure:

**Line Length**
```clojure
;; Soft limit: 80 characters (aim for this)
;; Hard limit: 120 characters (never exceed)

;; Break long function calls
(defn create-user [name email role permissions active? created-at]
  ...)  ; Too long - break it

;; Better - multiple lines
(defn create-user
  [name email role permissions active? created-at]
  ...)

;; Or with destructuring
(defn create-user
  [{:keys [name email role permissions active? created-at]}]
  ...)
```

**Spacing Around Forms**
```clojure
;; No space inside parentheses
(+ 1 2)     ; Good
( + 1 2 )   ; Bad

;; Single space between elements
[1 2 3]     ; Good
[1  2  3]   ; Bad - extra spaces

;; Single space after comma in maps (if using commas)
{:a 1, :b 2}   ; Good (commas are optional)
{:a 1,:b 2}    ; Bad - no space after comma
{:a 1 :b 2}    ; Also good - no commas needed
```

**Blank Lines**
```clojure
;; Separate top-level forms with blank line
(defn foo []
  ...)

(defn bar []
  ...)

;; Group related definitions
(def max-retries 3)
(def retry-delay 1000)

(defn with-retry [f]
  ...)

;; Blank line after ns form
(ns myapp.core
  (:require [clojure.string :as str]))

(defn my-function []
  ...)
```

**No Trailing Whitespace**
```clojure
;; Bad - trailing spaces at end of lines
(defn foo []   
  (bar))  

;; Good - no trailing whitespace
(defn foo []
  (bar))
```

**Commas Are Whitespace**
```clojure
;; Commas are optional - used for readability
{:a 1 :b 2 :c 3}        ; Without commas (common)
{:a 1, :b 2, :c 3}      ; With commas (also fine)
[1 2 3 4 5]             ; Vector - never use commas

;; Useful for visual grouping
{:name "Alice", :age 30,
 :email "alice@example.com"}
```

**Map Formatting**
```clojure
;; Single line for short maps
{:a 1 :b 2}

;; Multi-line with aligned values (optional)
{:name    "Alice"
 :age     30
 :email   "alice@example.com"
 :active? true}

;; Multi-line without alignment (also fine)
{:name "Alice"
 :age 30
 :email "alice@example.com"
 :active? true}

;; Keys on own lines for very long values
{:query
 "SELECT * FROM users WHERE status = 'active'"
 :params
 [user-id org-id]}
```

**Function Definition Formatting**
```clojure
;; Short function - single line
(defn double [x] (* x 2))

;; Medium function - docstring and body
(defn greet
  "Returns a greeting string."
  [name]
  (str "Hello, " name "!"))

;; Multi-arity
(defn greet
  "Greet with optional custom greeting."
  ([name]
   (greet "Hello" name))
  ([greeting name]
   (str greeting ", " name "!")))
```

**Breaking Long Forms**
```clojure
;; Long if - put condition, then, else on separate lines
(if (and (valid-user? user)
         (has-permission? user :admin))
  (grant-access user)
  (deny-access user))

;; Long let - one binding per line
(let [users (fetch-users db)
      active (filter :active? users)
      sorted (sort-by :name active)]
  (render-users sorted))

;; Long threading
(->> data
     (filter some-long-predicate-name?)
     (map transform-with-long-name)
     (reduce complicated-reducer initial-value))
```
What documentation conventions should I follow in Clojure?

Clojure has conventions for documenting code using docstrings and comments:

**Docstrings**
```clojure
;; Every public function should have a docstring
(defn calculate-tax
  "Calculates tax for the given amount.
  
  Takes an amount and tax rate, returns the tax.
  If no rate provided, uses default rate of 0.08."
  ([amount] (calculate-tax amount 0.08))
  ([amount rate] (* amount rate)))

;; Access docstrings
(doc calculate-tax)
```

**Docstring Format**
```clojure
;; Brief description on first line
;; Blank line, then details
(defn process-data
  "Processes raw data and returns normalized result.
  
  Arguments:
    data - A map with :items and :metadata keys
    opts - Optional map with :strict? and :validate? keys
  
  Returns a map with :result and :errors keys.
  
  Example:
    (process-data {:items [1 2 3]} {:strict? true})
    ;; => {:result [...] :errors []}
  
  Throws ExceptionInfo if data is malformed."
  [data & [opts]]
  ...)
```

**Namespace Docstrings**
```clojure
(ns myapp.api.handlers
  "HTTP API request handlers.
  
  This namespace contains Ring handlers for the REST API.
  All handlers follow the pattern of taking a request map
  and returning a response map.
  
  See myapp.api.routes for route definitions."
  (:require [ring.util.response :as resp]))
```

**Comments**
```clojure
;; Single semicolon for end-of-line comments
(def max-size 1000)  ; Maximum allowed size

;; Double semicolon for standalone comments
;; This function handles the main logic
(defn process []
  ...)

;;; Triple semicolon for section headers
;;; User Management Functions

(defn create-user []
  ...)

(defn delete-user []
  ...)
```

**When to Use Comments vs Docstrings**
```clojure
;; Use docstrings for:
;; - Public API documentation
;; - Function purpose and usage
;; - Argument descriptions
;; - Return value descriptions
;; - Examples

;; Use comments for:
;; - Implementation notes
;; - TODO/FIXME markers
;; - Explaining complex logic
;; - Temporary notes

(defn complex-algorithm
  "Finds optimal path using A* algorithm."
  [graph start end]
  ;; Priority queue ordered by f-score
  (let [open-set (priority-queue)]  ; TODO: Use better data structure
    ;; Main loop - continue until destination found or exhausted
    (loop [current start
           visited #{}]
      ;; Implementation note: We check bounds here because
      ;; the graph may contain invalid references
      ...)))
```

**Rich Comment Blocks**
```clojure
;; For REPL-driven development examples
(comment
  ;; Try these in the REPL:
  
  (create-user {:name "Alice" :email "a@b.com"})
  ;; => {:id 1 :name "Alice" :email "a@b.com"}
  
  (find-user 1)
  ;; => {:id 1 :name "Alice" ...}
  
  ;; Edge cases
  (create-user {})
  ;; => throws validation error
  )
```

**Spec as Documentation**
```clojure
(require '[clojure.spec.alpha :as s])

;; Specs serve as executable documentation
(s/def ::name (s/and string? #(< 0 (count %) 100)))
(s/def ::email (s/and string? #(re-matches #".+@.+\..+" %)))
(s/def ::age (s/and int? #(< 0 % 150)))

(s/def ::user
  (s/keys :req-un [::name ::email]
          :opt-un [::age]))

(s/fdef create-user
  :args (s/cat :user ::user)
  :ret ::user)
```

**Metadata for Documentation**
```clojure
;; Add metadata for additional docs
(defn ^{:doc "Creates a new user."
        :added "1.0"
        :deprecated "Use create-user-v2 instead"
        :see-also '[update-user delete-user]}
  create-user
  [data]
  ...)

;; Common metadata keys
^:private      ; Not part of public API
^:dynamic      ; Can be rebound
^:const        ; Compile-time constant
^:deprecated   ; Marked for removal
```
What are the best practices for organizing a Clojure project structure?

Here's how to organize a Clojure project following community conventions:

**Standard Project Structure**
```
my-project/
├── deps.edn              ; Dependencies (Clojure CLI)
├── project.clj           ; Dependencies (Leiningen, if using)
├── README.md
├── LICENSE
├── .gitignore
├── src/
│   └── my_project/       ; Note: underscores in directories
│       ├── core.clj      ; Main entry point
│       ├── config.clj    ; Configuration
│       ├── db.clj        ; Database layer
│       └── api/
│           ├── handlers.clj
│           └── routes.clj
├── test/
│   └── my_project/
│       ├── core_test.clj
│       └── api/
│           └── handlers_test.clj
├── resources/
│   ├── config.edn        ; Config files
│   └── public/           ; Static files
├── dev/
│   └── user.clj          ; REPL development helpers
└── target/               ; Build output (gitignored)
```

**deps.edn Configuration**
```clojure
{:paths ["src" "resources"]
 
 :deps {org.clojure/clojure {:mvn/version "1.11.1"}
        ;; Web
        metosin/reitit {:mvn/version "0.7.0"}
        ring/ring-core {:mvn/version "1.10.0"}
        ;; Data
        metosin/malli {:mvn/version "0.13.0"}
        com.github.seancorfield/next.jdbc {:mvn/version "1.3.883"}
        ;; JSON
        metosin/jsonista {:mvn/version "0.3.7"}}
 
 :aliases
 {:dev {:extra-paths ["dev" "test"]
        :extra-deps {cider/cider-nrepl {:mvn/version "0.30.0"}
                     hashp/hashp {:mvn/version "0.2.1"}}}
  
  :test {:extra-paths ["test"]
         :extra-deps {lambdaisland/kaocha {:mvn/version "1.87.1366"}}
         :main-opts ["-m" "kaocha.runner"]}
  
  :build {:deps {io.github.clojure/tools.build {:git/tag "v0.9.6" :git/sha "..."}
          :ns-default build}}}}
```

**Namespace Organization**
```clojure
;; src/my_project/core.clj - Entry point
(ns my-project.core
  "Application entry point."
  (:require [my-project.config :as config]
            [my-project.server :as server]))

(defn -main [& args]
  (server/start! (config/load-config)))

;; src/my_project/config.clj - Configuration
(ns my-project.config
  "Application configuration management.")

(defn load-config []
  (-> "config.edn" slurp edn/read-string))

;; src/my_project/db.clj - Database layer
(ns my-project.db
  "Database access functions."
  (:require [next.jdbc :as jdbc]))

;; src/my_project/api/handlers.clj - HTTP handlers
(ns my-project.api.handlers
  "HTTP API request handlers."
  (:require [my-project.db :as db]))

;; src/my_project/api/routes.clj - Route definitions  
(ns my-project.api.routes
  "API route definitions."
  (:require [my-project.api.handlers :as handlers]))
```

**Common Module Patterns**
```clojure
;; Layered architecture
my-project/
├── api/          ; HTTP layer
│   ├── handlers.clj
│   ├── routes.clj
│   └── middleware.clj
├── domain/       ; Business logic
│   ├── users.clj
│   └── orders.clj
├── db/           ; Data access
│   ├── core.clj
│   ├── users.clj
│   └── orders.clj
└── utils/        ; Shared utilities
    ├── time.clj
    └── validation.clj
```

**Dev Namespace**
```clojure
;; dev/user.clj - Loaded automatically by REPL
(ns user
  "Development helpers."
  (:require [my-project.core :as core]
            [my-project.config :as config]
            [clojure.tools.namespace.repl :refer [refresh]]))

(def system nil)

(defn start []
  (alter-var-root #'system
    (constantly (core/start-system (config/load-config)))))

(defn stop []
  (when system
    (core/stop-system system)
    (alter-var-root #'system (constantly nil))))

(defn reset []
  (stop)
  (refresh :after 'user/start))
```

**Test Organization**
```clojure
;; test/my_project/core_test.clj
(ns my-project.core-test
  (:require [clojure.test :refer [deftest is testing]]
            [my-project.core :as core]))

(deftest integration-test
  (testing "system starts and stops"
    (let [system (core/start-system test-config)]
      (is (some? system))
      (core/stop-system system))))

;; test/my_project/api/handlers_test.clj  
(ns my-project.api.handlers-test
  (:require [clojure.test :refer [deftest is testing use-fixtures]]
            [my-project.api.handlers :as handlers]
            [my-project.test-helpers :as helpers]))

(use-fixtures :each helpers/with-test-db)

(deftest create-user-test
  (testing "creates user with valid data"
    (let [response (handlers/create-user test-request)]
      (is (= 201 (:status response))))))
```

**Resource Organization**
```
resources/
├── config.edn           ; Default config
├── config/
│   ├── dev.edn          ; Dev overrides
│   ├── test.edn         ; Test config
│   └── prod.edn         ; Production config
├── db/
│   └── migrations/      ; SQL migrations
├── public/              ; Static web files
│   ├── css/
│   ├── js/
│   └── index.html
└── templates/           ; HTML templates
```
